newsitem.title: USA: Board recommends pay increase for AMR pilots.
newsitem.headline: Board recommends pay increase for AMR pilots.

text.p: President Clinton's emergency board on Wednesday recommended that AMR Corp's American Airlines give its pilots pay increases of 6.5 percent through 2000 to head off a strike, a White House statement said.

The Presidential Emergency Board also recommended additional limits on AMR's use of regional jets, but did not recommend that American's pilots in the Allied Pilots Association be asked to fly the regional jets.
The board also recommended gradual elimination of a lower pay scale for new hire pilots.
Clinton formed the three-member board on February 15 in response to a strike called by the pilots.
Although not legally binding on the parties, Clinton expressed the hope the recommendations would assist the parties in reaching a negotiated settlement.
"The best resolution is a negotiated settlement acceptable to both sides of this dispute," Clinton said.
It was not immediately certain if the mediators' recommendations were the basis of a tentative settlement that the pilots' union said be considered by its board on Friday.
If no settlement is reached by midnight on April 27, the pilots are free to strike and American is free to lock out its pilots or change their terms or conditions of employment, the statement said.
